items.followUp: State two features of the modern periodic table.

rubric.why: The table is arranged in order of increasing atomic number.
rubric.description: States the order of arrangement of elements.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that elements are arranged in increasing atomic-number order.

rubric.why: The long-form periodic table has seven periods and eighteen groups.
rubric.description: Gives the number of periods and groups.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark when both numbers are correct.

modelAnswer: Elements are arranged in order of increasing atomic number.
The table has 7 periods and 18 groups.

items.followUp: Define electron affinity and state the electron affinity of chlorine.

rubric.why: Electron affinity is the energy released when a gaseous atom gains an electron to form a negative ion.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the energy release associated with an atom accepting an electron.

rubric.why: The electron affinity of fluorine is approximately 328 kJ mol⁻¹.

modelAnswer: Electron affinity is the energy released when an isolated gaseous atom accepts an electron to form a negative ion.
The electron affinity of fluorine is approximately 328 kJ mol⁻¹.

items.followUp: Name four types of chemical bond.

rubric.why: Ionic and covalent bonds are two of the four types asked for.
Coordinate covalent and metallic bonds complete the four types.
rubric.description: Names coordinate covalent and metallic bonds.

modelAnswer: The four types are ionic, covalent, coordinate covalent and metallic bonds.

items.followUp: Explain how a covalent bond is formed.

rubric.description: Identifies sharing as the bonding process.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that electrons are shared.

rubric.why: A covalent bond is formed by sharing one or more pairs of electrons between atoms.
rubric.description: Identifies what is shared and between what.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for specifying electron pair(s) shared between atoms.

modelAnswer: A covalent bond is formed when two atoms share one or more pairs of electrons.

items.followUp: What is a polar covalent bond? Give an example.

rubric.why: In a nonpolar covalent bond, the bonding electrons are shared equally between the atoms.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the bonded atoms share electrons equally.

rubric.why: H₂ and Cl₂ are examples of nonpolar covalent molecules.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct example such as H₂ or Cl₂.

modelAnswer: A nonpolar covalent bond is a covalent bond in which the bonded atoms share the electron pair equally.
An example is the bond in an H₂ molecule.

items.followUp: What is the transition temperature of sulphur, and what change occurs at this temperature?

rubric.why: Transition temperature is the temperature at which one allotropic form changes into another.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing the temperature at which one form changes into another.

rubric.why: At about 95.6 °C, rhombic sulphur changes into monoclinic sulphur.
rubric.description: Gives the sulphur example and temperature.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct transition and approximate temperature.

modelAnswer: Transition temperature is the temperature at which one allotropic form of a substance changes into another.
At about 95.6 °C, rhombic sulphur changes into monoclinic sulphur.

rubric.why: An unsaturated solution contains less than the maximum amount of solute that can dissolve at that temperature.
rubric.description: States that the solution contains less than the maximum amount of solute.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for expressing that the solution is below its solubility limit.

rubric.why: An unsaturated solution can still dissolve more solute at the same temperature.
rubric.description: States that more solute can dissolve.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that additional solute can dissolve at that temperature.

modelAnswer: An unsaturated solution contains less than the maximum amount of solute that can dissolve at a given temperature.
It can dissolve more solute at that temperature.

items.followUp: Define reduction in terms of oxygen and give an example.

rubric.why: Oxidation, in terms of oxygen, is the addition of oxygen to a substance.
rubric.description: Defines oxidation in terms of oxygen.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that oxygen is added to a substance.

rubric.why: Magnesium forms magnesium oxide when it reacts with oxygen.
rubric.description: Gives a correct example of oxidation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a valid example, such as magnesium forming magnesium oxide.

modelAnswer: Oxidation, in terms of oxygen, is the addition of oxygen to a substance.
